messages:
Anya: ran the routing-config fuzzer against the latest console YAML authoring branch for ~2h, surfaced ~121 unique failures. dump attached but calling out the interesting classes: parse-error, ambiguous-header-match, precedence-surprise, wildcard-overlap. sample failing YAML below and a small repro command.

Anya: repro (run locally):\n```
./dev-tools/fuzz-runner --suite=routing-yaml --seed=4821 --target=console-parser
```

Anya: failing snippet that hit ambiguous-header (console accepted it but runtime disagreed):\n```
routes:\n  - match:\n      path: /api/*\n      headers:\n        X-Env: [prod, staging]\n        x-env: staging\n    action: forward:service-a
```

Mike: whoa, duplicate header keys with case diff. runtime normalizes headers to lowercase, console kept literal. does parser currently preserve original case? we should canonicalize earlier in the validation path. @Sahil any thoughts on schema-level guard vs parser normalization? :thinking_face:

Sahil: parser preserves source tokens for roundtrip; schema validation runs after parse so it saw two different keys and treated it as allowed. migration note: in schema-v3 we introduced header matchers that are case-insensitive at runtime. fix options: 1) parser canonicalize to lowercase and emit a lint warning when collisions happen, 2) validator reject duplicate-keys with case-insensitive compare, 3) console autofix by merging values. i prefer (2) for safety + a non-blocking autofix suggestion in console UI.

Mina: UX idea: when we detect case-insensitive dup keys, show a small inline hint with two actions: "Autofix (merge)" and "Keep as-is (warn)". Autofix should create a patch PR/TEMP edit and mark the route as needing review. Keep it opt-in for now. also log telemetry tag `route_yaml.duplicate_header_case` for counts.

Mike: ok for CI: should fuzz-run failures be hard-gates? i vote no for now — many are schema-compat issues caused by early rollout. propose CI rule: fuzz-run sets a metadata flag on PR and posts summary comment; fail only for parse-errors that indicate crash/exception. others produce warnings with counts. cc @ci-bot to post summary.

ci-bot: CI: fuzz-run summary for 1998765432 — duration 2h10m. total failures: 121. breakdown: parse-error: 9, ambiguous-header: 34, precedence-surprise: 48, wildcard-overlap: 30. top repro seeds: 4821, 4827, 4833. linking artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/fuzz/1998765432/report.html :robot_face:

Anya: precedence-surprise example — overlapping route weights + header override cascade:\n```
routes:\n  - match:\n      path: /api/v1/orders/*\n    action: forward:orders-v1\n  - match:\n      path: /api/*\n      headers:\n        X-Region: eu
    action: forward:eu-fallback
```

Anya: console preview showed the first route as more specific, but runtime applied header-scoped overrides that bumped the second route priority for some requests. this is an existing mismatch in the matching precedence doc. we need a small testsuite of combinatorial cases to lock behavior.

Sahil: i've got a failing unit test we can add to the matching engine repo. i'll push a reproducer to a feature branch and add a test matrix generator. also adding JSON schema upgrade compatibility: accept both `inverted` and `negate` for header-matcher for the next release and emit deprecation warning.

Mina: also think we should add a Console lint hint that says "Potential precedence mismatch — preview may differ from runtime for header-scoped wildcards." link to docs and an inline expand to show runtime vs preview diff. small copy: "Console preview uses simplified precedence heuristics; to be certain run `routingctl simulate` with your sample requests." :speech_balloon:

Mike: action items: @Mike -> add parser-level duplicate-key check + CI warning; @Sahil -> push unit tests + compat alias for field rename; @Mina -> mockups for inline autofix + telemetry events; @Anya -> upload full fuzz report and seeds to s3 and add a GH comment on the branch. I'll coordinate a small 2-day hotfix sprint next week. :thumbsup:

Anya: thanks — i'll attach the full report now and tag the PR.
